t:
Section 201(a) of said Act (53 Stat. 1279; 7 U.S.C. 1571(a)) is amended by adding at the end thereof a new paragraph (10), to read as follows:


“(10) 
The year and month beyond which an inoculant, if shown in the labeling, is no longer claimed to be effective.”

fable.w: This section only adds a labeling requirement about the expiration date of an inoculant's claimed effectiveness. There is no tempting reading here: it provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It is a substantive requirement on regulated parties, not a participation mechanism.
fable.s: The year and month beyond which an inoculant, if shown in the labeling, is no longer claimed to be effective.

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to require specific information on product labeling (the expiration date of an inoculant). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. It is a regulatory requirement for manufacturers, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: The year and month beyond which an inoculant, if shown in the labeling, is no longer claimed to be effective.

opus.w: This amendment only adds a required labeling item: the date after which an inoculant is no longer claimed to be effective. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. Labeling duties for sellers are a substantive rule, not a process for outside input. No consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be that a labeling rule involves regulators and industry, so it might count as participation. That fails here. The amendment only adds a new item to a seed-labeling list in Section 201(a) of the Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. 1571(a)). It doesn't create any comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to require specific information on product labels. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The requirement is a regulatory mandate for manufacturers, not a participatory process involving non-federal actors in the government's deliberations.
qwen_chat.s: The year and month beyond which an inoculant, if shown in the labeling, is no longer claimed to be effective.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring specific labeling information involves public participation because it informs consumers. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and more importantly, this section merely mandates a specific content requirement for product labels. It does not establish a process for the public, states, or other outside entities to consult with, comment on, or advise the federal government before a decision is made. The "participation" gate requires an outside party to be involved in the *decision-making process* (e.g., via hearings, advisory boards, or comment periods), not just to be the recipient of regulated information.
